what: The Debt Payoff Calculator builds a plan to clear several debts. It compares the avalanche method (highest interest rate first) with the snowball method (smallest balance first) and with paying only the minimums.
For each plan you see your debt-free date, the total interest, the interest saved and the order your debts are paid off. Your list is saved on this device so you can come back to it.
uses: See whether avalanche or snowball suits your debts.
Know the month you could be free of debt.
See how much an extra 50 or 100 a month saves.
Find debts whose minimum barely covers the interest.
Download the schedule and tick off each month.
tutorial: For each debt type a name, the "Balance", the "Interest (% per year)" and the "Minimum payment". Click "+ Add a debt" for more, or "Fill in an example" to try it.
Type the extra you can pay on top of all minimums in "Extra you can pay each month".
The cards show debt-free date, total interest and payoff order for avalanche, snowball and minimums only. The cheapest plan is highlighted.
The lines show your total balance falling over time for each plan.
Switch between avalanche and snowball in the table, then click "Download plan (CSV)".
features: Avalanche and snowball are calculated with the same monthly budget.
Freed-up minimums are added to the next target debt automatically.
Shows how long and how much interest without a plan.
Shows the difference against paying only minimums.
Interest is charged monthly at the yearly rate ÷ 12.
Your debts stay in this browser, never uploaded.

example.title: Worked example
example.text: A credit card (4,500 at 22.9%, minimum 135), a store card (900 at 27%, minimum 30), a car loan (12,000 at 7.5%, minimum 310) and a personal loan (3,000 at 11.5%, minimum 95) with 100 extra a month. Both plans clear everything in about 3 years 1 month, but avalanche pays about 235 less interest than snowball because it attacks the 22.9% card before the 11.5% loan.

tips: Never miss a minimum payment on any debt while following the plan.
Even a small extra amount every month shortens the plan a lot.
If two debts have similar rates, snowball's quick wins may be worth the small extra cost.
Check whether any debt has a promotional 0% rate ending soon and enter the rate it will become.
Avoid adding new debt while you pay off the old.
problems: It says the debt would never be paid off
Your payments do not cover the interest. Raise the minimum payments or the extra amount.
A red message names one debt
That row is missing a balance, rate or minimum payment, or a number is out of range.
My lender's numbers are slightly different
Lenders may charge interest daily, add fees or change the minimum each month. Treat this as a close estimate.
